bark.note: dark grey to blackish, cracked in a horizontal-reticulate pattern; inner bark red

canopy.silhouette: dense round crown over arching stilt roots

growth.juvenile_note: Viviparous, with the genus' biggest propagules: a heavy, warty, green club-shaped hypocotyl 36-64 cm (sometimes over 1 m) long hangs from the fruit. It spears into mud or floats, roots in a couple of weeks and opens a pair of leaves at the top. The sapling is a single stem with big glossy leaves ending in a sharp point (mucro), soon propped on arching stilt roots.
growth.source: ICRAF Agroforestree Database (to 27-30 m; hypocotyl 36-64 cm, sometimes over 100 cm; 35-40 yr to reach 19 cm diameter in Malaysia; 40-yr rotations; wind-pollinated, self-compatible); Wikipedia (20-25 m on riverbanks, 10-15 m on sea fringes); first flowering, rooting time and lifespan estimated

fruiting.source: ICRAF Agroforestree (inflorescences (1-)3-5(-12)-flowered; hard cream calyx 13-19 mm, 4 white hairy petals 9 mm; fruit 5-7 cm; hypocotyl 36-64 cm; wind-pollinated and self-compatible); fruit size given for the hanging propagule; months to maturity, set, crop and decay estimated from the genus

bark.note: grey-brown, rough, fissured and flaking in small patches

canopy.silhouette: spreading drooping crown over cone roots

growth.juvenile_note: Not viviparous: tiny seeds float out of the rotting fruit and germinate on mud. Seedling with 2 small cotyledons, then opposite, thick, round leathery leaves on a slender stem. Within a year or two it sends out horizontal cable roots with pencil-like breathing roots (pneumatophores) poking up through the mud around it, later becoming stout conical pegs 20-50 cm tall.
growth.source: Wikipedia Sonneratia alba (tree to 40 m, white flowers pink at the base, dark-green fruit to 5 cm); Tomlinson, The Botany of Mangroves (non-viviparous seed, pneumatophores, night flowers pollinated by bats and hawkmoths); growth, first seed and lifespan estimated for a pioneer mangrove

fruiting.source: Tomlinson, The Botany of Mangroves, and Wikipedia Sonneratia: flowers open at dusk and last one night, a big puff of white stamens with tiny petals, visited by nectar bats (Eonycteris, Macroglossus) and hawkmoths; flattened round green berry to 5 cm sitting on a star-shaped calyx, eaten raw or cooked; timing and counts estimated

growth.juvenile_note: Cryptoviviparous: the pale grey-green, heart-shaped propagule falls, sheds its skin within days and opens two thick fleshy cotyledons while hairy roots anchor it in the mud. The seedling is a slim stem with opposite, glossy green leaves that are silvery-grey beneath; pencil-like pneumatophores soon ring the young tree, which branches low into a bushy shrub.
growth.source: Almahasheer et al. 2016 Sci. Rep. 6:37785 (Red Sea growth: ~9.6 nodes/yr, internodes 5-11 cm/yr); Duke 1990 J. Ecol. (latitudinal phenology); seedling-bank behaviour from Australian studies; height-growth timings, first flowering and lifespan estimated.

fruiting.source: Almahasheer et al. 2016 Sci. Rep. (Red Sea: buds from June, peak flowering Nov, propagules ~3 months after flowering, released by April); Duke 1990 (flowering-to-fruit-fall lengthens with latitude, to ~1 yr in temperate Australia/NZ); propagules eaten after soaking/roasting; fruit set and crop estimated.

bark.note: seedling stem: smooth, green-grey with small lenticels (entry is the propagule stage)

ground.silhouette: single thin stem with a few leaves

growth.juvenile_note: Viviparous: the seed sprouts on the tree and a green, pencil-like hypocotyl 20-30 cm long hangs from the brown fruit. It drops, floats (weeks, up to a year), lodges upright in mud, roots from the lower tip within days and opens a pair of glossy leaves at the top. The sapling is a single stem that soon throws down arching red-brown prop roots.
growth.source: Tropical Plants Database (theferns.info) Rhizophora mangle (1-1.5 m/yr on productive sites; 5-20 m, rarely 30; flowers year-round; flowering by 6 yr, even 3-5 yr at 0.5-1 m tall; propagules 8-30 cm); Wikipedia (to 24 m, commonly ~6 m; propagules may float over a year); lifespan and shade estimated

fruiting.source: Tropical Plants Database (flowers all year; bees and wind; 4-7 months from fertilization to hypocotyl emergence plus 4-6 months more before it falls; propagules 8-30 cm); Wikipedia (pale yellow flowers; self or wind pollination); fruit size given for the hanging propagule; set, crop and decay estimated

bark.note: submerged; short vertical shoots from a buried rhizome

growth.juvenile_note: Seeds about 1 cm long are released when the ripe fruit splits and root within days on the sandy bottom. The seedling is a short shoot of 2-5 flat, bright-green ribbon leaves with rounded tips, anchored by a few thick roots; it grows a buried rhizome and after a year or two starts sending up new leaf shoots, spreading into a patch.
growth.source: Wikipedia Thalassia testudinum (leaves to 30 cm x 2 cm; rhizomes 5-10 cm deep; flowers Apr-Jul; fruit 20-25 mm with 1-6 seeds, splitting after ~8 weeks; low-tide mark to 30 m). Seed germination without dormancy, shoot lifespan (up to ~10-15 yr by leaf-scar ageing) and seedling-to-flowering time estimated from seagrass literature.

growth.juvenile_note: The germinating seed's hypocotyl swells at once into a tiny ball that roots onto spongy paperbark, topped by a pair of leaves. The ball grows into a knobbly, spiny, grey-brown caudex honeycombed inside with smooth and warted chambers that golden ants move into; a short thick stem on top carries a tuft of leathery leaves and tiny white tubular flowers and translucent white berries.
growth.source: Wikipedia Myrmecodia beccarii (epiphyte on Melaleuca and other spongy-barked trees in N Queensland wetlands and mangroves; prickly swollen caudex with hollows housing Philidris ants; white tubular flowers to 10 mm, white translucent one-seeded fruit); growth rates and ages estimated from ant-plant cultivation

growth.juvenile_note: Seedlings are tiny, silvery, grass-like tufts that hold no water. Over years the leaf bases widen into a big open tank rosette up to about 1 m across of broad, pale-green, often purple-tinged leaves; it flowers once on a branched stalk up to ~2 m tall with small white flowers, sets thousands of plumed seeds and then dies without making pups.
growth.source: Wikipedia Tillandsia utriculata (largest Florida tank bromeliad, holding up to a litre of water; devastated by the Mexican bromeliad weevil); Florida bromeliad accounts (monocarpic, no offsets, reproduces only by seed; tall branched inflorescence with white flowers). Growth and age at flowering estimated.

growth.juvenile_note: Hypogeal germination: the flat whitish seed stays at the mud surface while a shoot with pairs of opposite glossy leaves rises. The young plant is a single soft green stem with holly-like spiny-lobed leaves (leaves grown in shade are often entire and spineless); stems soon lean over, root where they touch the mud and build thickets.
growth.source: PROSEA Acanthus (continuous growth with no resting buds, non-seasonal flowering, hypogeal germination, clumps spread vegetatively); NUS Mangrove guidebook (erect to 2.5 m, spines strongest in exposed plants); growth years and stem life estimated

fruiting.source: Raju et al. 2017 Transylv Rev Syst Ecol Res 19.3 (large-bee pollination, natural fruit set <30%, fruits mature within a month, capsule splits explosively, 4 seeds); PROSEA (flowers last 2 days, sunbirds and insects, non-seasonal); Wikipedia (flowers 3-4 cm, terminal spikes to 16.5 cm, capsule 2.5-3 cm)
